blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Preference optimization has become a central approach for aligning large language models with human values, but its effectiveness depends heavily on the quality of preference annotations. In practice, preference data is often noisy due to annotation errors and ambiguity. Existing robust preference optimization methods primarily operate at the sequence level, implicitly treating entire responses as uniformly correct or incorrect. However, rejected responses may still contain informative reasoning steps, while preferred responses can include subtle errors. In this work, we propose \textbf{P}reference \textbf{O}ptimization via \textbf{R}obust \textbf{T}oken-level reweighting \textbf{(PORT)}, a fine-grained framework for robust alignment under noisy preferences. PORT performs token-level reweighting using the empirical cumulative distribution function (CDF) of token log-probabilities, yielding an efficient forward-pass-only proxy to gradient-norm penalization that selectively suppresses corrupted tokens without additional backward-pass computation. We provide theoretical analysis showing that PORT reduces the gradient bias from noisy preference labels by minimizing an upper bound on the bias term. Extensive experiments across diverse noise settings demonstrate that PORT consistently improves robustness and outperforms existing sequence-level baselines. The code is available at https://github.com/osu-srml/PORT
blocks.zh: 偏好优化已成为将大型语言模型与人类价值观相配合的核心方法,但其有效性在很大程度上取决于偏好说明的质量. 在实践中,由于注释错误和含糊不清,偏好数据往往很吵. 现有的强力偏好优化方法主要在序列层面运作,含蓄地将整个响应都视为统一正确或不正确. 然而,被拒绝的答复可能仍然包含内容丰富的推理步骤,而首选的答复可能包括微妙的错误。 在这项工作中,我们提出\textbf{P} 首选\textbf{O} 通过\textbf{R} obust\textbf{T} 重新加权\textbf{(PORT)} , 一个在吵闹的首选下强力对齐的精细框架 。 PORT利用符号日志概率的实证累积分配函数(CDF)进行符号级再加权,从而产生高效的只通过前行的代名词来进行梯度-规范惩罚,有选择地压制被腐蚀的符号而不进行额外的后行计算. 我们提供理论分析,表明PORT通过将偏好词上方的束缚最小化,从而从吵闹的偏好标签中减少梯度偏好. 不同噪音环境的广泛实验表明,PORT不断改进稳健性并超越现有序列级基线。 该代码可在https://github.com/osu-srml/PORT上查阅。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Preference optimization has emerged as a leading method for aligning large language models (LLMs) with human values, ensuring their outputs are useful, safe, and consistent with user intent [ 2 ] . Unlike Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) [ 18 ] , which trains an explicit reward model and then applies reinforcement learning to guide the policy toward high-reward responses, preference optimization methods such as Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) [ 20 ] and Identity Preference Optimization (IPO) [ 7 ] directly optimize the implicit reward margin between preferred and rejected responses within a stable, supervised learning paradigm.
blocks.zh: 优待优化已成为将大型语言模型(LLMs)与人类价值观接轨,确保其输出有用,安全,符合用户意图[2]的主导方法. 与强化从人类反馈学习(RLHF)[18]不同的是,它训练一种明确的奖励模式,然后应用强化学习来指导政策向高回报响应的方向发展,偏好优化方法如直接偏好优化(DPO)[20]和身份偏好优化(IPO)[7]在一个稳定,有监督的学习范式中直接优化偏好和拒绝的响应之间的隐含奖励幅度.

blocks.en: Despite their success, preference optimization methods share a key vulnerability: their effectiveness depends critically on the quality of preference annotations. In practice, however, preference data is rarely clean, and acquiring high-quality data at scale is often costly and even infeasible. Annotator disagreement, intrinsic ambiguity in hard-to-distinguish pairs, and labeling errors all introduce noise into the training signal, which biases gradient estimates and degrades alignment performance. To address this, recent work has explored mitigation techniques such as label smoothing [ 4 , 13 , 16 ] , regularization [ 15 , 26 ] , and heuristic data filtering [ 8 , 17 ] (see Appendix A for a discussion of each).
blocks.zh: 尽管取得了成功,但优化优惠的方法也具有关键的脆弱性:其效力关键取决于优惠说明的质量。 然而,在实践中,偏好数据很少干净,大规模获取高质量数据往往成本高昂,甚至不可行。 注释者不同意,在难以区分的对子中固有的模糊性,加上标注错误,都给训练信号引入噪音,这偏向了梯度估计,降低了校正性能. 为了解决这一问题,最近的工作探索了减缓技术,如标签平滑[4、13、16]、规范化[15、26]和热度数据过滤[8、17](关于每个问题的讨论见附录A)。

blocks.en: However, these approaches are fundamentally limited by their reliance on sequence-level modeling of preference noise. Existing preference optimization objectives and their noise-mitigation variants aggregate per-token log-ratios uniformly across an entire response, implicitly treating all token positions as equally reliable. This assumption is often violated in practice: a preferred response may contain localized hallucinations or reasoning errors, while a rejected response may still include correct intermediate reasoning steps.
blocks.zh: 然而,这些方法由于依赖于偏好噪声的序列级模型而从根本上受到限制. 现有的优化偏好目标及其减轻噪音的变体在整个反应中一致地累积了每桶对数-ratios,含蓄地将所有象征性位置视为同样可靠。 这种假设在实践中经常被违反:偏好的反应可能包含局部的幻觉或推理错误,而被拒绝的反应可能仍然包括正确的中间推理步骤.

blocks.en: Consider a preference pair where the preferred response is “The capital of Australia is Canberra, which was purpose-built as a compromise between Sydney and Melbourne,” while the rejected response is “The capital of Australia is Sydney, as it is the largest city.” If the preference label is flipped due to noise, sequence-level methods would penalize all tokens in the rejected response equally. However, this treatment is overly coarse: although the response is factually incorrect, many tokens (e.g., “as it is the largest city”) are locally fluent and not directly responsible for the error. Penalizing all tokens uniformly therefore introduces unnecessary bias into the learning signal, allowing noisy or uninformative tokens to disproportionately influence the gradient.
blocks.zh: 如果首选反应是“澳大利亚的首都是堪培拉,这是作为悉尼和墨尔本之间的妥协而专门建造的,而被拒绝的反应是“澳大利亚的首都是悉尼,因为它是最大的城市”。 如果偏好标签因噪声而翻转,序列级方法将同样惩罚被否决的响应中的所有符号. 然而,这种处理过于粗糙:虽然答复事实上是不正确的,但许多信物(如“最大的城市”)是当地流利的,对错误没有直接责任。 因此,统一惩罚所有标志,给学习信号带来不必要的偏差,使噪音或非信息信号对梯度产生不成比例的影响。

blocks.en: Unfortunately, existing noise mitigation strategies fail to resolve this mismatch. Label smoothing methods such as Conservative-DPO (cDPO) [ 16 ] apply uniform shrinkage to the entire objective, effectively scaling all token contributions equally. Pair-level reweighting methods such as Distributionally Robustifying DPO (Dr.DPO) [ 26 ] assign a single scalar weight to each preference pair, leaving within-sequence variation unmodeled. Even token-level importance sampling methods such as Token-Level Importance Sampling (TIS-DPO) [ 14 ] introduce finer granularity but rely on external reward models, thereby reintroducing risks of reward misgeneralization and additional computational overhead. Collectively, these limitations highlight a key gap: existing methods either operate at too coarse a granularity or depend on external supervision to achieve token-level adaptivity.
blocks.zh: 不幸的是,现有的减少噪音战略未能解决这种不匹配。 Conservative-DPO(cDPO)[16]等标签平滑方法对整个目标实行统一缩水,有效平摊所有象征性贡献. 配对级重置方法,如分布式强力DPO(Dr.DPO)[26]为每对首选配对分配一个单级的重力,留下序列内变数未建模. 甚至象Token-Level重要性抽样(TIS-DPO)[14]这样的象征性重要性抽样方法也引入了更细微的颗粒性,但依赖于外部奖励模型,从而再次引入奖励错误概括和额外计算间接费用的风险。 这些限制共同突出了一个关键差距:现有方法要么在颗粒性太粗糙的情况下运作,要么依赖外部监督来实现象征性的适应性。

blocks.en: Motivated by this, we explore token-level noise mitigation under instance-dependent preference noise and propose P reference O ptimization via R obust T oken-level reweighting (PORT) , a framework that performs token-level reweighting without requiring external reward models or additional backward passes. The key idea is to assign a weight to each token position such that solving a weighted preference optimization on noisy data yields a solution that aligns with true human preferences.
blocks.zh: 以此为动机,我们探索在依实例而定的偏好噪声下,通过R obust T oken级再加权(Port)进行标语级再加权(Port)的参考O刺激,这个框架不需要外部奖励模式或额外的落后通行证。 关键的想法是给每个标志位置分配一个权重,这样,在吵闹的数据上解决加权偏好优化就会产生一个符合人类真正偏好的解决办法。

blocks.en: To ground this design in theory, we analyze the effect of noise on the gradient of preference optimization and derive an upper bound on the resulting gradient bias. Minimizing this bound yields a closed-form optimal token-level weighting function, which characterizes how each token should be reweighted according to its sensitivity to noise and its contribution to the learning signal.
blocks.zh: 为了从理论上确定这种设计,我们分析噪音对偏好优化梯度的影响,并在由此产生的梯度偏差上得出上限. 最小化这个绑定产生一个封闭式的最佳符位加权功能,它特征是每个符位应该如何根据其对噪声的敏感性及其对学习信号的贡献重新加权.

blocks.en: However, this optimal solution is not directly computable in practice, as it depends on unknown noise statistics and the norm of the gradient with respect to all the model parameters which is computationally expensive. To bridge this gap, we identify a practical surrogate that preserves the structure of the optimal solution. In particular, we show that the relative ordering of token probabilities within a batch provides a sufficient signal for approximating the optimal weights. This leads to a CDF-based weighting scheme computed from model log-probabilities, which serves as an efficient and fully forward-pass–based proxy for the theoretically optimal solution.
blocks.zh: 然而,这一最佳解决办法在实践中并不能够直接计算,因为它取决于未知的噪音统计数据和所有计算成本的模型参数的梯度规范。 为了弥补这一差距,我们确定了一种实用的替代物,保留最佳解决方案的结构。 特别是,我们表明,一个批次内象征性概率的相对顺序,为接近最佳重量提供了足够信号。 这导致了一个基于CDF的权重方案,从模型的对数概率中计算出来,作为理论上最优解决方案的一个高效和完全前传的代名词。

blocks.en: Our main contributions are as follows: • We propose PORT , a robust alignment framework that introduces a token-level CDF reweighting objective that requires zero additional backward-pass overhead and no external reward model. • We provide theoretical guarantees showing that our weighting scheme minimizes an upper bound on gradient bias under instance-dependent noise, and characterize the conditions under which it strictly reduces the bias. • We conduct extensive experiments on Anthropic HH and Alpaca Farm benchmarks, demonstrating consistent and significant improvements over sequence-level baselines across diverse noise settings.
blocks.zh: 我们的主要贡献如下: 我们提议PORT,一个强有力的调整框架,引入一个象征性的CDF再加权目标,要求零增加后向通行费用,不采用外部奖励模式。 我们提供理论保障,表明我们的权重方案在依实例而定的噪音下,尽量减少梯度偏差的上限,并描述严格减少偏差的条件。 我们对Anthropic HH和Alpaca Farm基准进行了广泛的实验,表明在各种噪音环境的序列一级基线方面有连贯和重大的改进。

We hypothesize that the relative difference in the cumulative distribution function (CDF) of logits within a batch can serve as such a proxy. To formalize this idea, consider a batch containing B B preference pairs ( x [ b ] , y ~ w [ b ] , y ~ l [ b ] ) (x^{[b]},\tilde{y}_{w}^{[b]},\tilde{y}_{l}^{[b]}) . We will generate the response from the model trained with different baselines and then use the PKU Beaver evaluation model [ 5 ] to evaluate whether the response is safe or not. Across all baselines, PORT achieves the highest PKU-Beaver SR of 0.55 \mathbf{0.55} and GPT Win Rate of 67.6 % \mathbf{67.6\%} . blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en: In this work, we presented PORT (Preference Optimization via Robust Token-level reweighting), a fine-grained framework for robust LLM alignment under noisy preference annotations. Unlike existing sequence-level methods or approaches relying on external reward models, PORT performs token-level reweighting via the empirical CDF of token logits — a lightweight, forward-pass-only proxy requiring no additional backward-pass overhead. Theoretically, we derived the optimal weighting function by minimizing an upper bound on the noise-induced gradient bias, and established sufficient conditions under which PORT is guaranteed to strictly reduce this bias under both ϵ \epsilon -mislabeled and α \alpha -uncertain noise models. Empirically, we demonstrated through extensive experiments on AlpacaFarm, Anthropic HH, and PKU-Beaver that PORT consistently outperforms a broad range of sequence-level baselines across diverse noise settings and model architectures.
blocks.zh: 在这项工作中,我们提出了PORT(通过Robust Token级重新加权实现优待优化),这是在吵闹的优待说明下进行强力LLM调整的精细框架. 与依赖外部奖励模型的现有序列级方法或方法不同,PORT通过对令牌日志的经验CDF进行令牌级重新加权——一种轻量级的,仅限前传的代理,不需要额外的后传-过行管理费. 理论上,我们通过最小化噪音引起的梯度偏差上方的上方束缚,得出了最佳的权重功能,并建立了足够的条件,保证PORT在 \\ epsilon - mislabeled and α\ alpha - 不确定的噪音模型下严格减少这种偏差. 从经验上讲,我们通过对AlpacaFarm、Anthropic HH和PKU-Beaver的广泛实验,证明PORT在各种噪声环境和模型结构中,一贯超越一系列广泛的序列级基线。

blocks.en: A.1 Preference-based Alignment for Large Language Models
blocks.zh: A.1 对大语文模式的优先排序

blocks.en: Aligning large language models with human preferences has become a central problem in modern NLP [ 31 ] . Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) [ 18 ] is one of the most widely used approaches, where a reward model is trained from human annotations and then used to guide policy optimization. Despite its success, RLHF requires training an additional reward model and performing reinforcement learning, which makes the pipeline complex and unstable.
blocks.zh: 在现代NLP[31]中,将大型语言模型与人类偏好一致成为中心问题. 强化从人类反馈学习(RLHF)[18]是最广泛使用的方法之一,从人类说明中培训奖励模式,然后用来指导政策优化。 尽管取得了成功,RLHF要求培训额外的奖励模式和进行强化学习,这使得管道变得复杂和不稳定.

blocks.en: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) [ 20 ] has recently been proposed as a simpler alternative that directly optimizes the policy using pairwise preference data without explicitly training a reward model. DPO formulates preference learning using a Bradley–Terry model [ 3 ] and optimizes a supervised objective that implicitly regularizes the policy toward a reference model. Subsequent works [ 7 , 15 ] have extended DPO with different objectives, regularization strategies, and theoretical analyses, demonstrating competitive performance with improved stability. While these methods have significantly advanced alignment quality, they share a common assumption that is rarely satisfied in practice: the availability of clean, noise-free preference annotation [ 25 ] .
blocks.zh: 直接优惠优化(DPO)[20]最近被提出来作为比较简单的替代方案,直接利用双向优惠数据优化政策,而没有明确培训奖励模式. DPO用Bradley-Terry模型制定偏好学习,并优化了监督目标,将政策含蓄地规范化,以建立参考模型。 随后的作品[7,15]以不同的目标,规范化策略和理论分析扩展了DPO,展现了竞争表现,提高了稳定性. 虽然这些方法大大提高了对齐质量,但它们有一个共同的假设,在实践中很少满足:提供干净、无噪声的首选注释[25]。

blocks.en: A.2 Robust Preference Optimization under Noisy Feedback
blocks.zh: A.2 在噪音反馈下大力优化优惠

blocks.en:
Annotating large-scale preference datasets remains costly and labor-intensive, inevitably compromising annotation quality. Empirical studies suggest that 20%-40% of preference annotations in commonly used datasets contain labeling errors [ 13 ] , underscoring the practical severity of this problem.
Researchers have increasingly recognized the importance of noise robustness in preference alignment, leading to a growing body of work on robust DPO variants.
blocks.zh:
说明大规模优惠数据集的费用仍然很高,而且劳力密集,不可避免地损害说明的质量。 经验研究表明,常用数据集中20%-40%的首选说明含有标签错误[13],强调了这一问题的实际严重性.
研究人员越来越认识到噪声稳健性在调整优惠方面的重要性,导致关于强力DPO变体的工作越来越多。

blocks.en: One line of work addresses noise through label smoothing. Conservative-DPO (cDPO) [ 16 ] incorporates a conservative smoothing term that down-weights the influence of potentially flipped labels, providing provable robustness guarantees under bounded noise rates. Robust Preference Optimization (ROPO) [ 13 ] extends this with an adaptive smoothing mechanism that adjusts the correction strength based on estimated noise levels. However, both methods apply a uniform correction across all tokens in a response, failing to account for token-level variation in annotation quality.
blocks.zh: 一行工作通过标签平滑处理噪音. Conservative-DPO (cDPO) [16] 包含一个保守的平滑术语,将可能翻转的标签的影响降低重量,在限噪率下提供可证明的强性保证. 强偏好优化(ROPO)[13]扩展了这一功能,并采用了适应性平滑机制,根据估计噪声水平调整校正强度. 但是,这两种方法在答复中对所有符号都适用统一更正,没有说明注释质量中的符号级别差异。

blocks.en: A second line of work addresses noise through data filtering. Filtered DPO [ 17 ] employs a pretrained reward model to score each preference pair and filters out samples whose reward margin falls below a threshold. Adaptive batch-Wise SAMple Scheduling (SAMS) [ 8 ] utilizes a batch-wise training sample scheduling method to dynamically and adaptively schedule training samples. While effective, these approaches reintroduce the computational overhead and misgeneralization risks of reward-model-dependent pipelines, and may discard entire pairs even when only a subset of tokens are corrupted.
blocks.zh: 第二行的工作是通过数据过滤处理噪音问题。 被过滤的DPO [17] 使用经过预先训练的奖励模式来对每对优惠进行评分,并过滤出奖励幅度低于门槛的样品. 适应性批量-Wise SAMPLE排程(SAMS)[8] 采用分批培训样本排程法,动态和适应性地安排培训样本。 这些办法虽然有效,但又重新引入了依赖奖励模式的管道的计算间接费用和一般化错误的风险,甚至有可能在只有一小部分信物被腐蚀时丢弃整对信物。

blocks.en:
A third line addresses noise through reweighting, Distributionally
Robustifying DPO (Dr.DPO) [ 26 ] assigns pair-level weights based on estimated noise rates to reduce the influence of corrupted samples. Winsorized Direct Preference Optimization (wDPO) [ 15 ] applies Winsorized reweighting at the sequence level to limit the influence of outlier preference pairs. Im and Li [ 9 ] provide a theoretical analysis of how preference optimization generalizes under noisy feedback, characterizing the conditions under which noise degrades alignment quality. While these reweighting approaches improve robustness, they remain sequence-level methods that assign a single
scalar weight to each response pair, ignoring within-sequence token-level variation.

blocks.en: A.3 Token-level Modeling and Fine-grained Alignment
blocks.zh: A.3 建模和精细调整

blocks.en:
A parallel line of work has explored token-level modeling as a finer-grained alternative to sequence-level preference optimization. TDPO [ 30 ] proposes a token-level DPO formulation that decomposes the preference signal across individual tokens, allowing the objective to reflect each token’s contribution to the overall preference. Most closely related to our work, TIS-DPO [ 14 ] introduces
token-level importance sampling weights estimated from an external reward model, achieving fine-grained noise mitigation at the token level. However, TIS-DPO
inherits the limitations of reward-model-dependent approaches: it requires an additional model for weight estimation, introducing both computational overhead
and misgeneralization risk. LLMDoctor [ 22 ] proposes flow-guided token-level preference optimization for test-time alignment, while TIDPO [ 29 ] uses token importance scores derived from attention weights
to guide the preference optimization objective.

并行的工作线探索了象征级模型,作为序列级偏好优化的更精细的替代方案. TDPO[30]提出一个符号级的DPO表述,将各个符号的偏好信号分解,使目标能够反映每个符号对总体偏好的贡献. 与我们的工作最密切相关的是,TIS-DPO[14]介绍
从外部奖励模型中估算的标志级重要取样权重,在标志级上实现精细的噪声减缓. 然而,土耳其旅游局
继承了依赖奖励模式的方法的局限性:它要求增加一个重量估计模型,引入两种计算间接费用
和错误概括的风险。 LLMDoctor [22] 为测试时间对齐而提出流导符号级偏好优化,而TIDPO [29] 则使用由注意力权重衍生的符号重要性分数.

blocks.en: Motivated by these observations, we study preference optimization under noisy feedback from a token-level perspective. Instead of assigning a single weight to each pair, we design a token-level weighting mechanism that estimates the relative quality of each token using the empirical distribution of logits within the batch. This enables more accurate identification of corrupted regions and leads to improved robustness compared to sequence-level methods.
blocks.zh: 基于这些观察,我们研究在响亮的反馈下从象征性的角度优化偏好。 我们不给每对配对分配一个单一的重量,而是设计一个符号级的加权机制,利用批次内对数的经验分布来估计每个符号的相对质量. 这使得能够更准确地识别腐败地区,并导致与序列级方法相比增强稳健性。

Datasets. We conduct experiments on three benchmarks spanning helpfulness and safety alignment. AlpacaFarm [ 6 ] is a simulated human feedback
dataset designed for evaluating instruction-following alignment methods. It provides
a standardized training and evaluation pipeline that allows for reproducible
comparisons across methods. We use this dataset as our primary benchmark for
evaluating general alignment quality, reporting both Gold Reward Model (RM) Score
and GPT preference win rate as evaluation metrics. Anthropic HH [ 1 ] is a large-scale human preference
dataset covering two complementary alignment objectives: helpfulness and harmlessness.
The helpfulness split consists of 43,835 training samples and 2,354 test samples,
while the harmlessness split consists of 42,537 training samples and 2,312 test
samples. We use the harmlessness split to train models for safety alignment
evaluation, following the protocol of Dai et al. [5] . PKU-Beaver [ 10 ] is a large-scale safety benchmark providing fine-grained safety labels across multiple categories of harmful content, including violence, hate speech, self-harm, illegal activities, and misinformation. We use it only for evaluation, never as a training signal. Specifically, we sample 100 prompts from PKU-Beaver and use the same 100 prompts for every method. For each model trained on Anthropic HH, we generate one response per prompt. Each response is then evaluated in two ways. First, the PKU-Beaver safety classifier labels it as safe or unsafe, and the Safety Rate (SR) is the fraction of the 100 responses labeled safe. Second, GPT-4 compares it against the SFT model’s response to the same prompt using the pairwise protocol described below, which yields the GPT Win Rate reported for Anthropic HH. A higher SR indicates that the model more frequently produces safe responses when prompted with potentially harmful inputs. We use the PKU-Beaver safety classifier as an evaluator rather than a training signal: models trained on Anthropic HH are evaluated on PKU-Beaver prompts, with Safety Rate (SR) reported as the primary safety metric. A higher SR indicates that the model more frequently produces safe responses when prompted with potentially harmful inputs.

Evaluation metrics. We evaluate model performance using three complementary metrics. Gold Reward Model (RM) Score , GPT Win Rate (%) , and Safety Rate (SR) . Gold Reward Model (RM) Score measures response quality by
querying a large-scale human preference model [ 12 ] as a proxy for human judgment; following standard practice, we zero-center
the scores so that the initial reference policy has an average reward of
zero. GPT Win Rate (%) employs GPT-4 as a pairwise evaluator to
compare the output of each method against the SFT baseline; to mitigate
position bias, each pair is evaluated twice with the response order
swapped, and only consistent preferences are counted, inconsistent or tied judgments are excluded from the denominator. Safety Rate (SR) applies the PKU-Beaver safety
classifier [ 5 ] to responses generated on PKU-Beaver
prompts, reporting the fraction of responses deemed safe; a higher SR
indicates stronger alignment with harmlessness objectives.
Gold RM Score and GPT Win Rate are reported for AlpacaFarm, while
PKU-Beaver SR and GPT Win Rate are reported for Anthropic HH.

blocks.en: This work addresses the robustness of preference optimization under noisy human feedback, a fundamental challenge in aligning large language models with human values. By improving the reliability of alignment training, PORT has the potential to contribute to safer and more trustworthy AI systems, reducing the risk of models exhibiting harmful, biased, or misleading behaviors that can arise when training signals are corrupted. More broadly, our method lowers the annotation quality requirements for effective alignment, which may reduce the cost and labor burden of large-scale preference data collection and make robust alignment more accessible to resource-constrained practitioners.
blocks.zh: 这项工作解决了在吵闹的人类反馈下优化首选的稳健性问题,这是将大型语言模型与人类价值观相结合的根本挑战. 通过提高校准训练的可靠性,PORT有潜力为更安全和更值得信赖的AI系统做出贡献,降低模型显示在训练信号腐败时可能出现的有害,有偏见或误导行为的风险. 更广泛地说,我们的方法降低了对有效调整的注释质量要求,这可能减轻大规模优先数据收集的成本和劳动负担,并使资源紧张的从业人员更容易获得强有力的调整。

blocks.en: Despite these strengths, PORT has limitations worth noting: the CDF-based proxy relies on batch-level statistics and may be less reliable under very small batch sizes; and our theoretical guarantees hold under specific sufficient conditions that may not always be verifiable in practice. We hope PORT encourages future exploration of token-aware alignment approaches, including extensions to multi-turn settings and adaptive hyperparameter scheduling.
blocks.zh: 尽管有这些长处,PORT仍有一些局限性值得注意:基于CDF的代理依赖于批量级统计数据,在非常小的批量规模下可能不太可靠;我们的理论保证在具体的充分条件下存在,在实践中可能并不总是可以核实。 我们希望波特鼓励今后探索具有象征意义的调整方法,包括扩大多回合设置和适应性超参数的时间安排。

blocks.en: NeurIPS Paper Checklist
blocks.zh: 神经病 纸张核对表

blocks.en: 1. Claims Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope? Answer: [Yes] Justification: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper. 2. Limitations Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We add a limitation discussion in Appendix E . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. The authors should use their best judgment and recognize that individual actions in favor of transparency play an important role in developing norms that preserve the integrity of the community. Reviewers will be specifically instructed to not penalize honesty concerning limitations. 3. Theory assumptions and proofs Question: For each theoretical result, does the paper provide the full set of assumptions and a complete (and correct) proof? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We put the complete proof in the appendix. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include theoretical results. • All the theorems, formulas, and proofs in the paper should be numbered and cross-referenced. • All assumptions should be clearly stated or referenced in the statement of any theorems. • The proofs can either appear in the main paper or the supplemental material, but if they appear in the supplemental material, the authors are encouraged to provide a short proof sketch to provide intuition. • Inversely, any informal proof provided in the core of the paper should be complemented by formal proofs provided in appendix or supplemental material. • Theorems and Lemmas that the proof relies upon should be properly referenced. 4. Experimental result reproducibility Question: Does the paper fully disclose all the information needed to reproduce the main experimental results of the paper to the extent that it affects the main claims and/or conclusions of the paper (regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not)? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We put the hyperparameter we use in the appendix. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results. 5. Open access to data and code Question: Does the paper provide open access to the data and code, with sufficient instructions to faithfully reproduce the main experimental results, as described in supplemental material? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The dataset we use are all public, and we provide the code in the attached file. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that paper does not include experiments requiring code. • Please see the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • While we encourage the release of code and data, we understand that this might not be possible, so [No] is an acceptable answer. Papers cannot be rejected simply for not including code, unless this is central to the contribution (e.g., for a new open-source benchmark). • The instructions should contain the exact command and environment needed to run to reproduce the results. See the NeurIPS code and data submission guidelines ( https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy ) for more details. • The authors should provide instructions on data access and preparation, including how to access the raw data, preprocessed data, intermediate data, and generated data, etc. • The authors should provide scripts to reproduce all experimental results for the new proposed method and baselines. If only a subset of experiments are reproducible, they should state which ones are omitted from the script and why. • At submission time, to preserve anonymity, the authors should release anonymized versions (if applicable). • Providing as much information as possible in supplemental material (appended to the paper) is recommended, but including URLs to data and code is permitted. 6. Experimental setting/details Question: Does the paper specify all the training and test details (e.g., data splits, hyperparameters, how they were chosen, type of optimizer) necessary to understand the results? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We illustrate all the details in the experiment section. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The experimental setting should be presented in the core of the paper to a level of detail that is necessary to appreciate the results and make sense of them. • The full details can be provided either with the code, in appendix, or as supplemental material. 7. Experiment statistical significance Question: Does the paper report error bars suitably and correctly defined or other appropriate information about the statistical significance of the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We report the standard variance in table 2 . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The authors should answer [Yes] if the results are accompanied by error bars, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests, at least for the experiments that support the main claims of the paper. • The factors of variability that the error bars are capturing should be clearly stated (for example, train/test split, initialization, random drawing of some parameter, or overall run with given experimental conditions). • The method for calculating the error bars should be explained (closed form formula, call to a library function, bootstrap, etc.) • The assumptions made should be given (e.g., Normally distributed errors). • It should be clear whether the error bar is the standard deviation or the standard error of the mean. • It is OK to report 1-sigma error bars, but one should state it. The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text. 8. Experiments compute resources Question: For each experiment, does the paper provide sufficient information on the computer resources (type of compute workers, memory, time of execution) needed to reproduce the experiments? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We demonstrate the computation device we use in Appendix C.2 . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • The paper should indicate the type of compute workers CPU or GPU, internal cluster, or cloud provider, including relevant memory and storage. • The paper should provide the amount of compute required for each of the individual experimental runs as well as estimate the total compute. • The paper should disclose whether the full research project required more compute than the experiments reported in the paper (e.g., preliminary or failed experiments that didn’t make it into the paper). 9. Code of ethics Question: Does the research conducted in the paper conform, in every respect, with the NeurIPS Code of Ethics https://neurips.cc/public/EthicsGuidelines ? Answer: [Yes] Justification: There is no violation of the code of ethics. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the authors have not reviewed the NeurIPS Code of Ethics. • If the authors answer [No] , they should explain the special circumstances that require a deviation from the Code of Ethics. • The authors should make sure to preserve anonymity (e.g., if there is a special consideration due to laws or regulations in their jurisdiction). 10. Broader impacts Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed? Answer: [Yes] Justification: The social impact is written in Appendix D . Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML). 11. Safeguards Question: Does the paper describe safeguards that have been put in place for responsible release of data or models that have a high risk for misuse (e.g., pre-trained language models, image generators, or scraped datasets)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: No such risk. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper poses no such risks. • Released models that have a high risk for misuse or dual-use should be released with necessary safeguards to allow for controlled use of the model, for example by requiring that users adhere to usage guidelines or restrictions to access the model or implementing safety filters. • Datasets that have been scraped from the Internet could pose safety risks. The authors should describe how they avoided releasing unsafe images. • We recognize that providing effective safeguards is challenging, and many papers do not require this, but we encourage authors to take this into account and make a best faith effort. 12. Licenses for existing assets Question: Are the creators or original owners of assets (e.g., code, data, models), used in the paper, properly credited and are the license and terms of use explicitly mentioned and properly respected? Answer: [Yes] Justification: We cite the papers. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not use existing assets. • The authors should cite the original paper that produced the code package or dataset. • The authors should state which version of the asset is used and, if possible, include a URL. • The name of the license (e.g., CC-BY 4.0) should be included for each asset. • For scraped data from a particular source (e.g., website), the copyright and terms of service of that source should be provided. • If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset. • For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided. • If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators. 13. New assets Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not release new assets. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file. 14. Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)? Answer: [N/A] Justification: No crowdsourcing is involved. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector. 15. Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained? Answer: [N/A] Justification: The paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. • We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution. • For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review. 16. Declaration of LLM usage Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required. Answer: [N/A] Justification: We do not use LLMs as an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research. Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components. • Please refer to our LLM policy in the NeurIPS handbook for what should or should not be described.
blocks.zh: 一、导 言 索赔问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围? 答复:[是]理由: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指摘要和导言不包括文件中的主张。 抽象和(或)导言应明确说明所提出的要求,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 审议人员不会很好地看待对这一问题的[不]或[不]的答复。 所提出的主张应与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果可以归纳到其他场合。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。 2. 限制问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们在附录E中增加关于限制的讨论。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指文件没有限制,而答案[否]是指文件有限制,但在文件中没有讨论。 鼓励作者在论文中另辟一个“限制”部分。 文件应说明任何强有力的假设,以及这些假设遭到违反(例如,独立性假设、无噪声设置、模型精确度、不对称近似只在当地持有)的结果如何有力。 作者应思考这些假设在实践中可能如何遭到违反,其影响如何。 作者应思考所提出主张的范围,例如,如果这一办法只在几个数据集或几个运行中测试。 一般来说,经验性结果往往取决于隐含的假设,这些假设应当加以阐述。 作者应反思影响该办法执行的因素。 例如,一个面部识别算法在图像分辨率低或图像在低光照下拍摄时可能表现不佳. 或语音对文本系统可能无法可靠地用于为在线讲座提供闭门字幕,因为它无法处理技术术语。 作者应讨论提议的算法的计算效率以及它们如何用数据集大小来进行比例。 如果适用,作者应讨论他们处理隐私和公平问题的办法可能存在的局限性。 虽然作者可能担心审查人员会以完全诚实的限度作为拒绝的理由,但更糟糕的结果可能是审查人员发现文件中不承认的限制。 作者应运用最佳判断,承认有利于透明度的个别行动在制定维护社会完整性的规范方面发挥着重要作用。 将特别指示审查人员不要惩罚在限制方面的诚实。 3. 理论假设和证明 问题: 对于每一项理论结果,论文是否提供了一整套假设和完整的(和正确的)证明? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们把完整的证据放在附录里 准则: • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括理论结果. • 支助 所有论文中的定理,公式和证明,都应该编号,相互参照. • 支助 所有假设都应在任何定理的说明中明确说明或提及。 证据可以出现在主要论文或补充材料中,但如果在补充材料中出现,则鼓励作者提供简短的证据草图以提供直觉. • 反之,文件核心中提供的任何非正式证据都应辅以附录或补充材料中提供的正式证据。 • 应适当参考证据所依据的定理和莱玛。 4. 实验结果可复制 问题: 文件是否充分披露复制文件主要实验结果所需的所有信息,以影响文件的主要主张和/或结论(无论是否提供代码和数据)? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们把高参数 用于附录。 • 答案[N/A]是指论文不包括实验。 如果论文包括实验,审查人员将不会很好地看待对这一问题的回答: 使文件可以复制很重要,无论是否提供代码和数据。 如果资料是数据集和/或模型,作者应说明为使结果可以复制或可核查而采取的步骤。 • 根据贡献情况,可采用各种方式实现可复制性。 例如,如果这种贡献是一种新颖的架构,充分描述这种架构可能就足够了,或者如果这种贡献是一个具体的模型和经验性评价,那么就可能有必要使其他人能够用相同的数据集复制这个模型,或者提供对模型的访问. 总论中. 释放代码和数据往往是实现这一点的好办法,但也可以通过详细指示来提供可复制性,说明如何复制结果,访问主机模型(如在大语言模型的情况下),释放模型检查点,或者其他适合进行的研究的手段. • 支助 虽然NeurIPS不要求发布代码,但会议确实要求所有提交材料提供一些合理的可复制途径,这可能取决于贡献的性质. 例如(a) 如果贡献主要是一种新的算法,则论文应当明确说明如何复制该算法。 (b) 如果贡献主要是新的示范结构,文件应清楚、全面地描述这种结构。 (c) 如果贡献是一个新的模型(例如大语言模型),那么应该有一种方法来访问这个模型来复制结果,或者有一种方法来复制模型(例如,有一个开源数据集或关于如何构建数据集的指示). (d) 我们认识到,在某些情况下,可复制性可能很困难,在这种情况下,欢迎作者描述它们为可复制性规定的具体方式。 对于封闭源代码模型,可能以某种方式限制对模型的获取(如注册用户),但其他研究者应该有一定途径复制或验证结果. 5. 开放存取数据和代码 文件是否提供了开放的数据和代码,并有足够的指示,如补充材料所述,忠实地复制主要实验结果? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们使用的数据集都是公开的,我们在所附文件中提供了代码. · 答案[N/A]是指该文件不包括需要代码的实验。 详情请见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmission Policy)。 虽然我们鼓励发布代码和数据,但我们理解这也许是不可能的,因此[否]是一个可以接受的答案. 不能仅仅因为没有包含代码而拒绝文件,除非这是贡献的核心(例如,对于一个新的开源基准). • 支助 指示应包含复制结果所需的准确命令和环境。 详情见NeurIPS代码和数据提交准则(https://neurips.cc/public/guides/CodeSubmissionPolicy)。 作者应提供关于数据存取和准备的说明,包括如何获取原始数据、预先处理的数据、中间数据以及生成的数据等。 作者应提供脚本,复制所有实验结果,用于新的拟议方法和基线。 如果只有一组实验是可复制的,它们应该说明哪些实验从脚本中删除,以及为什么。 在提交来文时,为保持匿名,提交人应公布匿名版本(如果适用)。 • 建议在补充材料中提供尽可能多的信息(附于文件),但允许将URL纳入数据和代码。 6. 实验设置/细节问题: 文件是否具体说明了解结果所需的所有培训和测试细节(如数据分割、超参数、如何选择、优化者的类型)? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们说明了实验部分的所有细节。 • 答案[N/A]是指论文不包括实验。 实验环境应在文件核心中详细介绍,以便了解结果,使之合理。 详细情况可通过附录中的代码或补充材料提供。 7. 实验统计意义 问题: 纸质报告错误是否含有适当和正确定义的信息或关于实验统计意义的其他适当信息? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们在表2中报告标准差异。 • 答案[N/A]是指论文不包括实验。 如果结果附有错误栏、信任间隔或统计意义测试,至少对于支持论文主要主张的实验,作者应回答[是]。 应明确说明错误条所捕捉的可变因素(例如,列车/测试拆分、初始化、随机绘制某些参数,或在特定实验条件下的总体运行)。 计算错误栏的方法应加以解释(封闭格式公式、调用库函数、靴子陷阱等) —— 应给出假设(例如,通常分布错误)。 应明确误差栏是标准偏差还是平均值的标准误差. ^ 报告1-西格玛错误栏是正常的,但应该说明这一点。 如果错误的正常性假设没有得到核实,提交人最好报告2-西格玛错误栏,而不是说他们有96%的CI。 • 支助 对于不对称分布,作者应注意不要在表格或数字对称误差栏中显示会产生超出范围的结果(如负误差率). • 支助 如果在表格或图中报告错误栏,作者应在文字中解释它们是如何计算的,并在文字中参考相应的数字或表格。 8. 实验计算资源 问题:对于每个实验,论文是否提供了复制实验所需的计算机资源(计算工人类型,内存,执行时间)的充分信息? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们演示我们在附录C.2中使用的计算设备。 • 答案[N/A]是指论文不包括实验。 纸张应说明计算工人的CPU或GPU、内部集群或云提供商的类型,包括相关的内存和存储。 文件应提供每次试验所需的计算数额,并估计计算总额。 论文应披露完整的研究项目是否比论文中报告的实验需要更多的计算(例如初步或失败的实验,这些实验没有把它写进论文中). 9. 道德守则问题:文件中进行的研究是否在各个方面都符合《新IPS道德守则》(https://neurips.cc/public/Ethics Guidelines)? 答复:[是]理由: 没有违反道德守则。 • 答案[N/A]意味着作者没有审查《新IPS道德守则》。 如果作者回答[否],他们应该解释需要偏离道德守则的特殊情况。 提交人应确保匿名(例如,如果由于其管辖范围内的法律或条例受到特别考虑)。 10. 更广泛的影响问题:本文件是否讨论所开展工作的潜在积极社会影响和消极社会影响? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 社会影响载于附录D。 · 答案[N/A]是指所进行的工作没有社会影响。 如果作者回答[N/A]或[否],他们应当解释他们的工作为何没有社会影响,或为何文件没有涉及社会影响。 • 支助 负面社会影响的例子包括潜在的恶意或意外使用(例如:造谣、制造假面貌、监视)、公平考虑(例如:采用可能作出对特定群体造成不公平影响的决定的技术)、隐私考虑和安全考虑。 会议期望许多论文将是基础研究,而不是与特定应用挂钩,更不用说部署. 然而,如果有任何否定性申请的直接途径,提交人应当指出。 例如,可以合理地指出,可以利用基因模型质量的提高来产生用于造谣的Deepfakes. 另一方面,不需要指出优化神经网络的通用算法可以让人们训练出更快生成Deepfake的模型. ^ . 作者应考虑在技术作为预期和正确使用时可能产生的伤害,在技术作为预期使用时可能产生的伤害,但产生不正确的结果,以及(有意或无意)滥用技术造成的伤害。 如果存在负面的社会影响,作者还可以讨论可能的缓解战略(例如,对模型进行封闭释放,在攻击之外提供防御,监测误用的机制,监测系统如何从反馈中吸取教训的机制,提高ML的效率和可获取性)。 11. 保障问题: 文件是否描述了为负责任地发布具有高度滥用风险的数据或模型(如预先培训的语言模型、图像生成器或报废数据集)而实施的保障措施? 答复:[不详]理由: 没有这种风险。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件没有构成这种风险。 • 释放的具有高度滥用或双重用途风险的模型,应附带必要的保障措施,允许控制使用该模型,例如要求用户遵守使用准则或限制进入模型或实施安全过滤器。 • 支助 从互联网上拆掉的数据集可能构成安全风险。 作者应说明如何避免释放不安全的图像。 我们认识到,提供有效的保障是一项挑战,许多文件并不要求这样做,但我们鼓励作者考虑到这一点,并作出最大的诚意努力。 12. 现有资产的许可证问题: 纸上是否使用资产(例如代码、数据、模型)的创造者或原始所有人,是否适当贷记,许可证和使用条款是否明确提及和适当遵守? 答复:[是] 理由说明: 我们引用文件。 • 答案[N/A]是指该文件不使用现有资产。 作者应引述产生代码包或数据集的原始文件。 作者应说明使用哪个版本的资产,并在可能的情况下包括一个URL。 许可证名称(如CC-BY 4.0)应包含每项资产。 • 支助 对于从某一特定来源(如网站)提取的数据,应当提供该来源的版权和服务条件。 资产放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于流行的数据集来说,使用code.com/dataset的文档拥有一些数据集的许可证。 它们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。 • 支助 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。 如果这种信息不在网上提供,则鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。 13. 新资产问题:文件中介绍的新资产是否有详细记录,是否与资产一起提供文件? 答复:[不详]理由: 文件没有放出新的资产。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不释放新资产。 • 研究人员应通过结构化模板,将数据集/代码/模型的细节作为提交材料的一部分。 • 培训、许可证、限制等细节 该文件应讨论是否以及如何获得资产被使用者的同意。 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL 或包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。 14. 人口集中和人类课题研究 关于众包实验和与人类主体的研究,论文是否包括提供给参与者的指示全文和(如果适用的话)截图,以及(如果有)补偿的细节? 答复:[不详]理由: 没有涉及众包。 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 将这一资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人类主题,那么应在主要文件中尽可能详细。 • 支助 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、整理或其他工作的工人应至少领取数据收集国的最低工资。 15. 机构审查委员会(IRB)批准或相当于与人有关的研究 文件是否描述了研究参与者可能面临的风险,是否向主体披露了这些风险,以及是否获得了机构审查委员会的批准(或根据贵国或机构的要求获得同等的批准/审查)? 答复:[不详]理由: 论文不涉及众包,也不涉及人类主体的研究. 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 视进行研究的国家而定,任何人类课题研究可能需要IRB批准(或相当于批准)。 - 如果得到移民和难民局的批准,应在报纸上明确说明这一点。 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大不相同,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。 • 支助 对于初次提交材料,不包括任何可能打破匿名性的信息(如果适用的话),例如进行审查的机构。 16. 关于LLM使用的声明问题: 论文是否描述了LLMs的使用,如果它是本研究核心方法的重要、原始或非标准组成部分? 请注意,如果LLM只用于书写、编辑或格式化目的,且不影响研究的核心方法、科学严谨性或原创性,则不需要宣布。 答复:[不详]理由: 我们不使用LLMs作为这一研究的核心方法的重要、原始或非标准的组成部分。 · 答案[N/A]是指本研究的核心方法开发并不涉及作为任何重要、原始或非标准组成部分的法学硕士。 请参看NeurIPS手册中我们的LLM政策,说明应该或不应该描述什么。

blocks.en: Question: Do the main claims made in the abstract and introduction accurately reflect the paper’s contributions and scope?
blocks.zh: 问题: 抽象和导言中的主要主张是否准确地反映了文件的贡献和范围?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification:
blocks.zh: 理由说明:

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the abstract and introduction do not include the claims made in the paper. • The abstract and/or introduction should clearly state the claims made, including the contributions made in the paper and important assumptions and limitations. A [No] or [N/A] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers. • The claims made should match theoretical and experimental results, and reflect how much the results can be expected to generalize to other settings. • It is fine to include aspirational goals as motivation as long as it is clear that these goals are not attained by the paper.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指摘要和导言不包括文件中的主张。 抽象和(或)导言应明确说明所提出的要求,包括文件中的贡献以及重要的假设和限制。 审议人员不会很好地看待对这一问题的[不]或[不]的答复。 所提出的主张应与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果可以归纳到其他场合。 只要文件明确没有实现这些目标,就最好将理想目标作为动力列入。

blocks.zh: 所提出的索赔应当与理论和实验结果相符,并反映在多大程度上可以预期结果能够归纳到其他环境。

blocks.en: Limitations
blocks.zh: 限制

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper discuss the limitations of the work performed by the authors?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否讨论了作者所做工作的限制?

blocks.en: Answer: [Yes]
blocks.zh: 答复:[是]

blocks.en: Justification: We add a limitation discussion in Appendix E .
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 我们在附录E中增加关于限制的讨论。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper has no limitation while the answer [No] means that the paper has limitations, but those are not discussed in the paper. • The authors are encouraged to create a separate “Limitations” section in their paper. • The paper should point out any strong assumptions and how robust the results are to violations of these assumptions (e.g., independence assumptions, noiseless settings, model well-specification, asymptotic approximations only holding locally). The authors should reflect on how these assumptions might be violated in practice and what the implications would be. • The authors should reflect on the scope of the claims made, e.g., if the approach was only tested on a few datasets or with a few runs. In general, empirical results often depend on implicit assumptions, which should be articulated. • The authors should reflect on the factors that influence the performance of the approach. For example, a facial recognition algorithm may perform poorly when image resolution is low or images are taken in low lighting. Or a speech-to-text system might not be used reliably to provide closed captions for online lectures because it fails to handle technical jargon. • The authors should discuss the computational efficiency of the proposed algorithms and how they scale with dataset size. • If applicable, the authors should discuss possible limitations of their approach to address problems of privacy and fairness. • While the authors might fear that complete honesty about limitations might be used by reviewers as grounds for rejection, a worse outcome might be that reviewers discover limitations that aren’t acknowledged in the paper. blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not include experiments. • If the paper includes experiments, a [No] answer to this question will not be perceived well by the reviewers: Making the paper reproducible is important, regardless of whether the code and data are provided or not. • If the contribution is a dataset and/or model, the authors should describe the steps taken to make their results reproducible or verifiable. • Depending on the contribution, reproducibility can be accomplished in various ways. For example, if the contribution is a novel architecture, describing the architecture fully might suffice, or if the contribution is a specific model and empirical evaluation, it may be necessary to either make it possible for others to replicate the model with the same dataset, or provide access to the model. In general. releasing code and data is often one good way to accomplish this, but reproducibility can also be provided via detailed instructions for how to replicate the results, access to a hosted model (e.g., in the case of a large language model), releasing of a model checkpoint, or other means that are appropriate to the research performed. • While NeurIPS does not require releasing code, the conference does require all submissions to provide some reasonable avenue for reproducibility, which may depend on the nature of the contribution. For example (a) If the contribution is primarily a new algorithm, the paper should make it clear how to reproduce that algorithm. (b) If the contribution is primarily a new model architecture, the paper should describe the architecture clearly and fully. (c) If the contribution is a new model (e.g., a large language model), then there should either be a way to access this model for reproducing the results or a way to reproduce the model (e.g., with an open-source dataset or instructions for how to construct the dataset). (d) We recognize that reproducibility may be tricky in some cases, in which case authors are welcome to describe the particular way they provide for reproducibility. In the case of closed-source models, it may be that access to the model is limited in some way (e.g., to registered users), but it should be possible for other researchers to have some path to reproducing or verifying the results.

The authors should preferably report a 2-sigma error bar than state that they have a 96% CI, if the hypothesis of Normality of errors is not verified. • For asymmetric distributions, the authors should be careful not to show in tables or figures symmetric error bars that would yield results that are out of range (e.g., negative error rates). • If error bars are reported in tables or plots, the authors should explain in the text how they were calculated and reference the corresponding figures or tables in the text.

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper discuss both potential positive societal impacts and negative societal impacts of the work performed?

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that there is no societal impact of the work performed. • If the authors answer [N/A] or [No] , they should explain why their work has no societal impact or why the paper does not address societal impact. • Examples of negative societal impacts include potential malicious or unintended uses (e.g., disinformation, generating fake profiles, surveillance), fairness considerations (e.g., deployment of technologies that could make decisions that unfairly impact specific groups), privacy considerations, and security considerations. • The conference expects that many papers will be foundational research and not tied to particular applications, let alone deployments. However, if there is a direct path to any negative applications, the authors should point it out. For example, it is legitimate to point out that an improvement in the quality of generative models could be used to generate Deepfakes for disinformation. On the other hand, it is not needed to point out that a generic algorithm for optimizing neural networks could enable people to train models that generate Deepfakes faster. • The authors should consider possible harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended and functioning correctly, harms that could arise when the technology is being used as intended but gives incorrect results, and harms following from (intentional or unintentional) misuse of the technology. • If there are negative societal impacts, the authors could also discuss possible mitigation strategies (e.g., gated release of models, providing defenses in addition to attacks, mechanisms for monitoring misuse, mechanisms to monitor how a system learns from feedback over time, improving the efficiency and accessibility of ML).

blocks.en: If assets are released, the license, copyright information, and terms of use in the package should be provided. For popular datasets, paperswithcode.com/datasets has curated licenses for some datasets. Their licensing guide can help determine the license of a dataset.
blocks.zh: 资产放行的,应当提供许可证,著作权信息,包件中的使用条件. 对于流行的数据集来说,使用code.com/dataset的文档拥有一些数据集的许可证。 它们的许可证指南有助于确定一个数据集的许可证。

blocks.en: For existing datasets that are re-packaged, both the original license and the license of the derived asset (if it has changed) should be provided.
blocks.zh: 对于重新包装的现有数据集,应当提供原始许可证和衍生资产的许可证(如果已经改变)。

blocks.en: If this information is not available online, the authors are encouraged to reach out to the asset’s creators.
blocks.zh: 如果这种信息不在网上提供,则鼓励作者接触资产的创造者。

blocks.en: New assets
blocks.zh: 新资产

blocks.en: Question: Are new assets introduced in the paper well documented and is the documentation provided alongside the assets?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件中介绍的新资产是否有详细记录,是否与资产一起提供文件?

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: The paper does not release new assets.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 文件没有放出新的资产。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets. • Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc. • The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used. • At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指该文件不释放新资产。 • 研究人员应通过结构化模板,将数据集/代码/模型的细节作为提交材料的一部分。 • 培训、许可证、限制等细节 该文件应讨论是否以及如何获得资产被使用者的同意。 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL 或包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。

blocks.en: The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not release new assets.
blocks.zh: 答案[N/A]表示论文不释放新资产.

blocks.en: Researchers should communicate the details of the dataset/code/model as part of their submissions via structured templates. This includes details about training, license, limitations, etc.
blocks.zh: 研究人员应通过结构化模板,将数据集/代码/模型的细节作为其提交材料的一部分。 其中包括培训、许可证、限制等细节。

blocks.en: The paper should discuss whether and how consent was obtained from people whose asset is used.
blocks.zh: 文件应讨论是否以及如何获得资产被使用者的同意。

blocks.en: At submission time, remember to anonymize your assets (if applicable). You can either create an anonymized URL or include an anonymized zip file.
blocks.zh: 在提交时,请记住对您的资产进行匿名(如果适用)。 您可以创建一个匿名的 URL 或者包含一个匿名的 zip 文件 。

blocks.en: Crowdsourcing and research with human subjects
blocks.zh: 与人类学科的群包和研究

blocks.en: Question: For crowdsourcing experiments and research with human subjects, does the paper include the full text of instructions given to participants and screenshots, if applicable, as well as details about compensation (if any)?
blocks.zh: 问题: 关于众包实验和与人类主体的研究,论文是否包括提供给参与者的指示全文和(如果适用的话)截图,以及(如果有)补偿的细节?

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: No crowdsourcing is involved.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 没有涉及众包。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper. • According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 将这一资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人类主题,那么应在主要文件中尽可能详细。 • 支助 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、整理或其他工作的工人应至少领取数据收集国的最低工资。

blocks.en: The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects.
blocks.zh: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究.

blocks.en: Including this information in the supplemental material is fine, but if the main contribution of the paper involves human subjects, then as much detail as possible should be included in the main paper.
blocks.zh: 将这种资料列入补充材料是好的,但如果论文的主要贡献涉及人类主体,那么应在主要论文中尽可能详细.

blocks.en: According to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics, workers involved in data collection, curation, or other labor should be paid at least the minimum wage in the country of the data collector.
blocks.zh: 根据《新IPS道德守则》,从事数据收集、整理或其他工作的工人应至少领取数据收集国的最低工资。

blocks.en: Institutional review board (IRB) approvals or equivalent for research with human subjects
blocks.zh: 机构审查委员会(IRB)批准或相当于与人有关的研究

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper describe potential risks incurred by study participants, whether such risks were disclosed to the subjects, and whether Institutional Review Board (IRB) approvals (or an equivalent approval/review based on the requirements of your country or institution) were obtained?
blocks.zh: 问题: 文件是否描述了研究参与者可能面临的风险,是否向主体披露了这些风险,以及是否获得了机构审查委员会的批准(或根据贵国或机构的要求获得同等的批准/审查)?

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: The paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 论文不涉及众包,也不涉及人类主体的研究.

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects. • Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper. • We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution. • For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review.
blocks.zh: 准则: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究. • 视进行研究的国家而定,任何人类课题研究可能需要IRB批准(或相当于批准)。 - 如果得到移民和难民局的批准,应在报纸上明确说明这一点。 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大不相同,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。 • 支助 对于初次提交材料,不包括任何可能打破匿名性的信息(如果适用的话),例如进行审查的机构。

blocks.en: The answer [N/A] means that the paper does not involve crowdsourcing nor research with human subjects.
blocks.zh: 答案[N/A]是指论文不涉及众包或与人类主体的研究.

blocks.en: Depending on the country in which research is conducted, IRB approval (or equivalent) may be required for any human subjects research. If you obtained IRB approval, you should clearly state this in the paper.
blocks.zh: 根据开展研究的国家不同,任何人类课题研究可能需要IRB批准(或相当于). 如果你得到IRB的批准,你应该在报纸上清楚地说明这一点。

blocks.en: We recognize that the procedures for this may vary significantly between institutions and locations, and we expect authors to adhere to the NeurIPS Code of Ethics and the guidelines for their institution.
blocks.zh: 我们认识到,各机构和地点在这方面的程序可能大不相同,我们期望作者遵守《新IPS道德守则》及其机构准则。

blocks.en: For initial submissions, do not include any information that would break anonymity (if applicable), such as the institution conducting the review.
blocks.zh: 对于初次提交材料,不包括任何可能打破匿名性的信息(如适用的话),例如进行审查的机构。

blocks.en: Declaration of LLM usage
blocks.zh: 声明LLM的使用

blocks.en: Question: Does the paper describe the usage of LLMs if it is an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research? Note that if the LLM is used only for writing, editing, or formatting purposes and does not impact the core methodology, scientific rigor, or originality of the research, declaration is not required.
blocks.zh: 问题: 论文是否描述了LLMs的使用,如果它是本研究核心方法的重要、原始或非标准组成部分? 请注意,如果LLM只用于书写、编辑或格式化目的,且不影响研究的核心方法、科学严谨性或原创性,则不需要宣布。

blocks.en: Answer: [N/A]
blocks.zh: 答复:[不详]

blocks.en: Justification: We do not use LLMs as an important, original, or non-standard component of the core methods in this research.
blocks.zh: 理由说明: 我们不使用LLMs作为这一研究的核心方法的重要、原始或非标准的组成部分。

blocks.en: Guidelines: • The answer [N/A] means that the core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components. • Please refer to our LLM policy in the NeurIPS handbook for what should or should not be described.
blocks.zh: · 答案[N/A]是指本研究的核心方法开发并不涉及作为任何重要、原始或非标准组成部分的法学硕士。 请参看NeurIPS手册中我们的LLM政策,说明应该或不应该描述什么。

blocks.en: The answer [N/A] means that the core method development in this research does not involve LLMs as any important, original, or non-standard components.
blocks.zh: 答案[N/A]是指本研究中的核心方法开发并不涉及LLMs作为任何重要,原始,或非标准成分.

blocks.en: Please refer to our LLM policy in the NeurIPS handbook for what should or should not be described.
